style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm of the cup of salvation -- part of the Egyptian Hallel Jesus sang at the Last Supper, and the most personal thanksgiving in the set. It begins with a declaration rare in Scripture: 'I love the LORD' -- said plainly, and for a plain reason: He heard my voice; He bent His ear to me; therefore I will call on Him as long as I live. The rescue was from the very cords of death and the straits of Sheol, and the psalmist's theology of it is simple: gracious is the LORD, and righteous, and merciful; He guards the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me. Then the tender self-address -- return to your rest, O my soul, for the LORD has dealt bountifully with you -- and the walk resumed in the land of the living. The center asks the question every rescued person asks: what shall I give back to the LORD for all His benefits? And the answer is the psalm's genius: not a payment but a receipt -- I will lift the cup of salvation and call on His name; I will pay my vows in front of everyone. Verse 15 gives the church its epitaph for every believer's grave: precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His faithful ones. And the last verses walk the thanksgiving straight into the temple courts, in the middle of Jerusalem, with a hallelujah.

1.text: I love the LORD, because He hears my voice and my pleadings for grace.
1.amp: I love [ahab] the LORD [YHWH], because He has heard [shama] my voice [qol] and my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace].
1.notes: ahavti -- 'I love': the psalm opens with the verb Scripture usually reserves for God's side of the covenant, here confessed by a man about God. The reason is concrete and humble: shama (H8085), He heard -- tachanunim (H8469), the grace-pleas of one with no case but need.

2.text: Because He bent His ear down to me, I will keep calling on Him all my days.
2.amp: Because He has inclined [natah -- bent, stretched down] His ear [ozen] unto me, therefore will I call [qara] upon Him as long as I live ['in my days', yom, the KJV margin].
2.notes: natah ozen (H5186, H241): the ear bent down to a low speaker -- the posture of Psalm 40:1. The response is a lifetime resolution: be-yamai, in all my days, qara. One answered prayer converts a man into a permanent caller.

3.text: The cords of death wrapped around me, and the tight straits of Sheol found me; I found nothing but trouble and sorrow.
3.amp: The sorrows [chebel -- cords, ropes] of death [mavet] compassed [aphaph -- closed around] me, and the pains [metsar -- the narrows, the straits] of hell [sheol] got hold ['found me', matsa, the KJV margin] upon me: I found [matsa] trouble [tsarah] and sorrow [yagon].
3.notes: chebel mavet (H2256, H4194), death's ropes, and metsare sheol (H4712, H7585), the grave's narrow places -- the same tight-place word as Psalm 118:5. Two matsa's: the straits found him, and he found only tsarah and yagon (H6869, H3015). Death as a net that finds its man.

4.text: Then I called on the name of the LORD: 'O LORD, I plead with You -- rescue my soul!'
4.amp: Then called [qara] I upon the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH]; 'O LORD, I beseech [anna -- please!] You, deliver [malat -- let slip free, rescue] my soul [nephesh].'
4.notes: The prayer quoted whole, and it is short: anna YHWH, malletah naphshi -- please, LORD, let my soul slip free. malat (H4422) is escape from a closing grip; the whole theology of the psalm's rescue is one breath long.

5.text: Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; yes, our God is full of compassion.
5.amp: Gracious [channun] is the LORD [YHWH], and righteous [tsaddiq]; yea, our God [Elohim] is merciful [racham -- shows compassion].
5.notes: The doctrine distilled from the deliverance: channun, tsaddiq, racham (H2587, H6662, H7355) -- grace and compassion bracketing righteousness, Sinai's self-portrait (cf. Exodus 34:6) confirmed at one man's sickbed. 'OUR God' -- the private rescue immediately shared.

6.text: The LORD keeps watch over the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me.
6.amp: The LORD [YHWH] preserves [shamar -- guards] the simple [peti -- the open, the unguarded]; I was brought low [dalal], and He helped [yasha -- saved] me.
6.notes: The petaim (H6612) are the unsophisticated, the easily led -- the very people Proverbs warns; the LORD shamar (H8104) them anyway. dalal (H1809) is to hang low, be brought down thin: the psalmist claims the simple man's place and gets the simple man's rescue, yasha (H3467).

7.text: Go back to your resting place, O my soul, for the LORD has dealt generously with you.
7.amp: Return [shub] unto your rest [manoach -- your resting place], O my soul [nephesh]; for the LORD [YHWH] has dealt bountifully [gamal -- dealt out fully] with you.
7.notes: The tenderest self-address in the Psalter: shuvi nafshi li-menuchayekhi -- soul, go back to your resting place. manoach (H4494) is Noah's-ark word for the dove's perch (cf. Genesis 8:9): the storm is over, come back and land. gamal (H1580), the full-dealing verb of Psalm 13:6 and 119:17.

8.text: For You have rescued my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling.
8.amp: For You have delivered [chalats -- drawn out] my soul [nephesh] from death [mavet], mine eyes [ayin] from tears [dimah], and my feet [regel] from falling [dechi -- stumbling].
8.notes: Three rescues descending from ultimate to daily: nephesh from mavet, ayin from dimah, regel from dechi (H1762). chalats (H2502), the drawing-out verb: the same God who pulled him from death's ropes also keeps his feet on the path and his eyes dry.

9.text: I will walk about before the LORD's face in the lands of the living.
9.amp: I will walk [halak] before [panim] the LORD [YHWH] in the land [eretz] of the living [chay].
9.notes: The rescued man's itinerary: halak le-phne YHWH, walking before His face -- Abraham's charge (cf. Genesis 17:1) -- in artsot ha-chayyim, the lands of the living, which he had nearly left. Survival with an audience of One.

10.text: I kept believing, even when I said, 'I am greatly afflicted';
10.amp: I believed [aman -- held firm in faith], therefore have I spoken [dabar]: I was greatly [meod] afflicted [anah]:
10.notes: aman (H539), the faith-verb: belief that kept speaking even from inside the affliction. Paul quotes this line for the whole ministry of the gospel -- 'I believed, therefore I spoke' (cf. 2 Corinthians 4:13): faith is not silent about its troubles; it is not silent about its God either.

11.text: I said in my alarm, 'Every man is a liar.'
11.amp: I said [amar] in my haste [chaphaz -- my alarm, my panic] all men [adam] are liars [kazab].
11.notes: chaphaz (H2648) is panicked flight -- the word for hurried retreat. In it he indicted the race: kol ha-adam kozev, every man a liar, every human promise a broken reed. The verdict was hasty; it was also not entirely wrong (cf. Romans 3:4, Paul citing the same phrase). God alone did not lie to him.

12.text: What can I give back to the LORD for all His benefits toward me?
12.amp: What shall I render [shub -- return] unto the LORD [YHWH] for all His benefits [tagmul -- His dealings, His bounties] toward me?
12.notes: The question of every rescued life: mah ashib -- what can I RETURN? tagmulohi (H8408), from the same root as verse 7's gamal: the bounties dealt out, now begging a response. The answer in the next verse is the psalm's stroke of genius.

13.text: I will raise the cup of salvation high and call upon the LORD's name.
13.amp: I will take [nasa -- lift up] the cup [kos] of salvation [yeshuah], and call [qara] upon the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH].
13.notes: How do you repay a Rescuer? You take MORE from Him: nasa kos yeshuot (H3563, H3444), the cup of salvations lifted -- the thank-offering's libation, and the posture of a man who repays grace by receiving it publicly. Jesus lifted this cup at the Supper as the Hallel was sung (cf. Matthew 26:27-30; 1 Corinthians 10:16).

14.text: I will make good my vows to the LORD -- right now, in front of all His people.
14.amp: I will pay [shalam -- complete, make good] my vows [neder] unto the LORD [YHWH] now in the presence of all His people [am].
14.notes: shalam neder (H7999, H5088): the vow made in the straits paid in the open, neged na, right now and in public. Private bargains with God become public testimony -- the debt discharged where the congregation can hear the receipt read.

15.text: Precious in the eyes of the LORD is the death of His faithful ones.
15.amp: Precious [yaqar -- costly, weighty, rare] in the sight [ayin] of the LORD [YHWH] is the death [mavet] of His saints [chasid -- His covenant-loyal ones].
15.notes: The church's epitaph for its dead. yaqar (H3368) is preciousness by weight -- costly, not cheap: God does not spend His chasidim's lives carelessly, which is why this psalmist's death was refused (v. 8). And when the death does come, it comes weighed and valued in His ayin -- no saint dies unwatched (cf. Revelation 14:13).

16.text: O LORD, truly I am Your servant; I am Your servant, the son of Your handmaid -- You have loosed my bonds.
16.amp: O LORD [YHWH], truly [anna] I am Your servant [ebed]; I am Your servant, and the son [ben] of Your handmaid [amah]: You have loosed [pathach -- opened, untied] my bonds [moserah].
16.notes: The doubled avdekha and the ben amatekha: a house-born servant, belonging by birth, not purchase (cf. Exodus 21:5-6). The moserot (H4147) are the same bonds Psalm 2:3 shows the rebels tearing at -- here pathach (H6605), untied by the Master's own hand, so the freed slave stays. Loosed bonds produce a willing servant.

17.text: To You I will offer the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and I will call on the name of the LORD.
17.amp: I will offer [zabach] to You the sacrifice [zebach] of thanksgiving [todah], and will call [qara] upon the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH].
17.notes: The zebach todah (H2077, H8426), the thank-offering with its shared feast -- the cup of verse 13 poured out beside it. And 'call on the name of the LORD' for the third time in the psalm: calling in the straits (v. 4), calling with the cup (v. 13), calling at the altar. The rescued man's whole life becomes one continuous qara.

18.text: I will make good my vows to the LORD -- right now, in front of all His people,
18.amp: I will pay [shalam] my vows [neder] unto the LORD [YHWH] now in the presence of all His people [am],
18.notes: Verse 14 repeated word for word, as vows deserve -- said twice so the congregation can hold him to it. The location is about to be named.

19.text: in the courts of the house of the LORD, in the very midst of you, O Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
19.amp: In the courts [chatser] of the LORD'S [YHWH] house [bayith], in the midst [tavek] of you, O Jerusalem [Yerushalaim]. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
19.notes: The thanksgiving walks to its address: the chatsrot bet YHWH (H2691, H1004), be-tokhekhi Yerushalaim -- the temple courts in the city's heart, the place vows were paid. And the Hallel's signature closes it: halelu-Yah. A psalm that began 'I love' ends 'praise' -- the two verbs of a rescued life.
